title: Cannot use 'Win + Space' when swapping from PowerToys Run to Command Palette
author: maddie-j
summary: Command Palette’s Win+Space single/double-press behavior matches the older open cross-module Win+Space regression in #47660.

status.label: Duplicate of Win+Space regression
status.detail: #47660 covers the same language-switcher conflict across PowerToys Run, Command Palette, and Keyboard Manager.

next_action.label: Post duplicate guidance
next_action.reason: Consolidate current-version and low-level-hook observations in #47660.

judgment.rationale: The same Win+Space regression, including focus-dependent single/double presses and Command Palette reports, predates this issue in #47660.
evidence: Windows input switching wins unless low-level hooking is used in the original report.
Later reporters require a second Space even with low-level hooking.
#47660 has the same behavior and Command Palette/Keyboard Manager confirmations.
#39783 also documents Command Palette Win+Space needing low-level hook.
judgment.recommended_action: Post a duplicate comment directing current-version and hook-setting observations to #47660.

issue_context.summary: Win+Space is contested by the Windows language switcher, and Command Palette inconsistently receives it depending on focus and hook mode.
known_information: PowerToys Run previously handled the binding; Command Palette initially required low-level hook.
Later users say low-level mode no longer resolves it or two Space presses are required.
The issue has seven comments and no assignee.
inferences: Variation across machines may involve hook ordering or Windows input-language handling, but it does not need a separate track from #47660.
issue_context.analysis: The older issue already has the same behavior and broader modules. Consolidation is more useful than separate generic ZIP requests.
initial_investigation: #47660 predates this issue and describes first-press language switching and later-press PowerToys activation.
Its comments extend the regression to Command Palette and Keyboard Manager.
CmdPalKeyboardService/KeyboardListener.cpp implements the optional low-level hook path.
No fix closes either open issue.

actions.label: Post duplicate guidance

comment.body: Thanks for the detailed follow-ups. This matches the older open regression in #47660, which already tracks Win+Space being taken by the Windows language switcher on the first press, requiring another Space press for PowerToys, and affecting PowerToys Run, Command Palette, and Keyboard Manager. The newer reports here that low-level hook mode no longer changes the result are useful; please add current PowerToys/Windows versions and those observations to #47660 so the hook and focus variants stay in one investigation. Closing this issue as a duplicate of #47660.
